name: Opus Quality Defensive
strategy: Low-beta quality/defensive core (healthcare, quality factor, min-vol, staples) with a small gold diversifier and a disciplined 8% short on semis to express 'AI-infra overextended' without dominating the book.

positions.thesis: Healthcare: cheap, defensive, and actually leading the recent tape (+8.5% since April) - defense that participates.
Quality factor (high ROE, low leverage) participates in recoveries while screening out junk - fixes Round 1's over-defensiveness.
Min-vol core ballast; cut tariff-crash drawdown to -9% vs SPY -19% historically.
Low-volatility sleeve; best equity crash defender in backtest (-6.6% vs -19%).
Consumer staples: low-beta cash-flow ballast, held up in every drawdown window tested.
Small non-equity crash hedge - was +1.6% while stocks fell 19% in the tariff crash.
Disciplined short of overextended semis - the AI-overextension view, sized as insurance not a bet.

backtest.notes: Hedge genuinely defends (captured ~25-40% of downside in both crashes) but the book lags rising markets hard. Inverse leveraged ETFs rejected: SOXS lost 98% in the 2026 recovery; a plain 8% SMH short is the disciplined insurance.

outlook: With concentration extreme and semis parabolic, reward-to-risk in the AI trade keeps deteriorating; positioned to protect NAV in an unwind while participating via quality (XLV/QUAL).
